title: "Special Parameters: Positional, IFS, and PATH"

# Special Parameters: Positional, IFS, and PATH

Bash reserves single-character parameters for tracking runtime state, command-line arguments, and environment boundaries:

## Positional Arguments and `$@` vs `$*`

| Parameter | Meaning | Quoted Expansion |
|-----------|---------|------------------|
| `$0` | Name of the script or shell | `"$0"` |
| `$1` .. `$9` | Individual positional arguments | `"$1"` |
| `${10}` | Arguments beyond 9 require braces | `"${10}"` |
| `$#` | Number of positional arguments | `"$#"` |
| `$@` | All arguments as individual words | `"$@"` expands to `"$1" "$2" "$3"` (Safe) |
| `$*` | All arguments concatenated | `"$*"` expands to `"$1 $2 $3"` joined by `$IFS` |

```bash
# ALWAYS use "$@" when iterating over command-line arguments
for arg in "$@"; do
    echo "Processing: $arg"
done
```

## Process & Runtime Parameters

* `$?`: Exit status of the most recently executed foreground pipeline (0 = success).
* `$$`: Process ID (PID) of the current shell.
* `$!`: Process ID of the most recently spawned background process.
* `$_`: The last argument of the previous command executed.
